text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The window of opportunity on Cyprus runs risks of closing, U.N. envoy on Cyprus warns.
- The U.S. and Britain start important talks on the Cyprus issue.
- U.N. envoy on Cyprus passes (U.N. Secretary-General Kofi) Annan's message of concern about the situation on the island.
- Power failure livens up subdued session of parliament.
- U.N. envoy starts consultations aimed at preparing for direct negotiations between the two sides.
- Cypriots owe five billion pounds to banks, according to a trade union survey.
- The Central Bank of Cyprus insists it should control co-operative credit societies.
- Washington plays second fiddle to the United Nations on an initiative on Cyprus.
- Mass dismissals drive unemployment up by 22.6 percent compared to last year.
- Finance minister makes dramatic appeal to Cyprus Airways staff to avoid taking strike measures.
